newsitem.title: UK: Canada heads govt bond index in week - Salomon.
newsitem.headline: Canada heads govt bond index in week - Salomon.

text.p: Canadian bonds led the field in the Salomon world government bond index (WGBI) in the week to July 3, Salomon Brothers said on Friday.
Overall the WGBI gained 0.71 percent in local currency terms in a week in which none of the government bond markets listed made negative returns. In dollar terms the index gained 0.45 percent.
During the week the U.S. Federal Reserve kept interest rates on hold, a stance strengthened by a weaker than expected June employment report.

A rally in the Canadian dollar, still benefiting from the recent rise in Canadian interest rates, and the U.S. payrolls data on Thursday, helped boost Canadian bonds which gained 1.01 percent in local terms.
But in U.S. dollars, Irish government bonds outstripped them offering gains of 2.11 percent, compared with Canadian bonds' 1.47 percent.
Japanese government bonds (JGBs) also offered good gains, racking up 0.97 percent in yen terms and 1.09 percent in dollars.
British gilts made returns of 0.39 percent in sterling terms and offered a respectable 1.45 percent in dollars.
In continental Europe, Italian BTPs made gains of 0.62 percent in lira terms, but showed a loss of 0.20 percent in dollar terms.
German Bunds and French OATS also suffered in dollars. Bunds gained 0.30 percent and OATs 0.35 percent in local currency terms but both showed losses in dollars of 0.87 and 0.73 percent respectively.

Salomon's bond index is calculated using all government bonds with over one year to maturity, weighted for market capitalisation. Only bonds freely available to institutional investors and with a certain minimum amount outstanding are included. Returns take account of price moves and accrued interest.
